tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H18): Attribute and remove e1's ~19 us weight-path chain (M rows), carry the fix into e4. Step 0 (precision gate, owed from r1): run r1-merge's e1 and e4 paths on every row they serve (32,14,14 64,14,14 2,56,56 4,56,56 16,28,28 and the 5 L rows) over 10 seeds against an fp64 reference. Log max err/(atol+rtol|ref|) per row; the gate is 0.8. Step 1: add %globaltimer stamps to e1 (lane 0 of the producer, MMA and one epilogue warp) at kernel entry, phase-0 image done, grid-counter release, each weight unit landing (bar_full), GEMM1 done, batch-counter release, GEMM2 done and last store. Print the CTA-median and max at 1,28,28 and 64,14,14. Step 2: run the critic's ready hot-spot probe: 148 CTAs x 64 serial 32 KB bulk copies through S=1/3/6 stages, from one shared image vs 16 replicas vs private copies, after a 2xL2 zero_. Step 3: run_tests the already-written ring variant r1-a-e1-ts-fp16x3-ring (ring depth from t). Step 4: fix the largest term the stamps show: (a) replicas: phase 0 writes R=8-16 image copies and CTA i reads copy i%R, if the probe shows shared minus replica > 0.3 us/unit; (b) a deeper or finer ring (16 KB stages) if MMA waits on bar_full; (c) cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 of the image at entry; (d) if phase 0 plus the grid counter is > 3 us, convert-on-ingest weights so the grid barrier goes away. Step 5: apply the same producer change to e4 (r1-a-e4-rounds-tmem) and run_tests the L rows in the same container. Hand in both kernels. Success: e1 M rows -20% rented in the same container (64,14,14 <= 29 us, 2,56,56 <= 20 us), with the stamps showing which term moved; err/tol <= 0.8 on every row logged Refuted if: the stamps show weight units plus phase 0 make up < 30% of e1's chain at 1,28,28, and no weight-path variant moves any M row by more than 5% This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). A missed gate or success line is not a reason to stop: switch to the best configuration your own probes found (or the experiment's next variant), build it into a full kernel and measure it with run_tests, and use the rest of the budget on it. Hand in a measured kernel that implements this experiment's design on at least one workload (others may fall back); the r0 baseline or the unchanged parent is not a valid candidate unless a measured hardware fact rules the design out (name it, with the probe's number). Record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Keep the kernel copy-like (memory-bound): the portal locks the SM clock lower than the test bench and penalises extra SM work per byte (the problem card). Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic / bulk-reduce target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); any stored h or scratch is reused only within one call, never across calls; grid, cluster or per-batch counters live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only; TMA descriptors encoded every call; no state kept between calls (no converted or split weights, no cached outputs) except shape-keyed attributes set to one maximal value; cache hints only on our own workspace buffers, never on hidden_states, the weights or the output; cuobjdump -res-usage STACK 0 on the shipped build; 10-round fp64 precision log (err/tol) on every shipped row.

Experiment E2 (tests H19): Cluster-2 hidden-split pairs: two 128-token tiles of h per SM so GEMM1/GELU of tile i+1 overlaps the wait, pass 2 and GEMM2 of tile i (L). Step 0 (5 min): stamp e4 at 64,56,56 and 16,56,56 (globaltimer per round: x converted, each GEMM1 block committed, GELU done, batch counter released, pass 2 done, GEMM2 committed, out stored, and the MMA warp's total wait on bar_full). Record the fraction of the round the MMA is idle. Step 1: build the pair variant. Use a persistent one-wave grid of 74 clusters of 2 (check cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters >= 74 with your exact smem and the cooperative + cluster launch attributes; H17 says 74 at >=180 KB). CTA rank r owns hidden [256r, 256r+256). Per 128-token tile each SM runs 1SM swap-AB GEMM1 (2 hidden blocks x 128 token columns = 256 TMEM columns), using e4's GELU/sumsq epilogue on its 256 channels. Two tiles are resident (columns 0-255 and 256-511). Use rounds of 9408 tokens (3x3136 = 12x784 = 48x196, about 73.5 tiles, batch-aligned) so that each pair runs GEMM1 of round k+1 before waiting on round k's per-batch counters; this is deadlock-free because GEMM1 never waits on a counter. After the wait, pass 2 converts the tile's own 256 channels; the GEMM2 partial (out^T: M=128 outs, N=128 tokens, K=256 own hidden), with main and cross accumulators placed in that tile's freed h columns as e4 does. Then exchange halves through DSMEM (each SM sends 64 tokens x 128 outs = 32 KB, mbarrier complete_tx), add b2' and store its 64 tokens. Each SM streams only its half of the weights (256 KB per tile); keep W1 resident instead if smem allows. Step 2: run_tests on all L rows plus 16,28,28 and 4,56,56, interleaved with e4 in one container, and log err/tol over 10 seeds. Fallback if the pair build does not pass in time: cross-round overlap in e4 (I22: next round's x into R0 and GEMM1 blocks 2/3 into columns 256-511 during GEMM2 hb3 and the output drain), measured the same way. Success: pair kernel passes all served rows with err/tol <= 0.8 and runs L rows >= 35% faster than e4 rented (64,56,56 round-equivalent <= 1.5x its own MMA+exchange projection) Refuted if: step-0 stamps show the MMA idle < 25% of an e4 round (then overlap cannot pay), or the pair kernel at 64,56,56 is not >= 15% faster than e4 in the same container This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. Experiment E3 (tests H21): Fan-out for the 6272-token rows (TT=196 x 4 slices) plus stamps of the 3136-token rows. Step 0 (precision gate): log err/tol per row over 10 seeds (fp64 reference) for the 4 rows B serves. Step 1: stamp the 4,28,28 path with globaltimer (x and weights landed, GEMM1 committed, GELU+sumsq done, barrier released, x2 split done, GEMM2 committed, red.add done). Attribute the ~5 us gap between 784 and 3136 tokens. Step 2: add a TT=196 instance for 6272 tokens (2,56,56 and 32,14,14): 32 token tiles x 4 hidden slices = 128 CTAs, one wave. smem: x hi/lo 100 KB + W1 slice hi/lo 64 KB; after GEMM1 commits, bulk-copy the W2 slice hi/lo over W1; the x2 split reuses the x buffer. TMEM: D1 = 208 columns; keep h in TMEM if registers do not fit (the TT=98 instance is already at 125 regs); run GEMM2 in two token halves of 104 with main and cross accumulators (208 columns) beside D1. Keep red.add v4 into the b2-prefilled output (H15: bulk reduce is slower). Check sm_100a regs and spills before running. Step 3: run_tests on all 14 rows against r1-merge in one container; route only the rows this kernel wins. Step 4, if time remains and step 1 shows GELU+split > 3 us at 3136 tokens: vectorise the x2 split (transposed TMEM read, one 32-bit STS per 2 tokens) and re-measure the 3136 rows. Success: 2,56,56 and 32,14,14 <= 19 us rented (vs e1 25.3 / 28.3 in the same container), all served rows err/tol <= 0.8 Refuted if: TT=196 cannot fit without spills or a second wave, or both 6272 rows run > 23 us rented (under 10% better than e1) This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. Experiment E4 (tests H20): New design: two-launch stored-h FP16x3 pipeline with resident weight halves (L rows). You may read the r0 baseline and read_example's #129 token-stationary tcgen05 kernel (SW128 descriptors, idesc kind::f16, elect.sync issue, packed A&S gelu2). Step 0 (hardware premise, 10 min): a memory-only skeleton under the harness flush (2xL2 zero_). K1 reads x and writes 2 KB/token; K2 is launched with PDL (griddepcontrol, same stream), reads that back and writes out; no maths. Time it at 64,56,56, 32,56,56, 16,56,56 and 32,28,28. Expect about 150 / 78 / 40 / 20 us rented. Step 1, K1 (persistent, 148 CTAs): each CTA owns a hidden half (CTA parity) and keeps its W1 half as SW128 hi/lo in smem (128 KB, built in the prologue from fp32 W1 while the first x tile loads). Per 128-token tile: x hi/lo, GEMM1 FP16x3 swap-AB into one of two TMEM accumulators (2 x 256 columns, double-buffered so the epilogue of tile i overlaps the MMA of tile i+1), then a gelu2 epilogue. Write per-tile per-channel sumsq partials with plain stores (two slots when a tile straddles a batch: no atomics, no zeroing, no state across calls), and store h (fp32, or fp16 hi/lo of unscaled h) at 2 KB/token through smem plus bulk stores. Step 2, K2 (PDL): its prologue reduces the partials of its batch(es) into G, nf and s. Per 128-token tile, choose between (a) folding s into a per-batch W2'_b out-half held resident in smem (rebuilt only when the CTA's batch changes; gb W2 + b2 as an fp32 bias), so K2 is a pure TMA->MMA GEMM on h hi/lo, and (b) loading fp32 h by TMA, with converter warps applying x2 = h*s + gb and the split. Use FP16x3 with a separate GEMM2 cross accumulator. A crude first version may use 1SM N=64 out-halves; note in findings whether cta_group::2 pairs (each SM loads half the operand) are the next step. Allocate the h workspace with torch.empty in the binding (no fills). The kernel must be correct for every shape; route only the rows where it wins. Step 3: run_tests on all rows interleaved with r1-merge, and log err/tol over 10 seeds for the L rows. Success: 64,56,56 <= 170 us rented and every L row >= 10% faster than e4 in the same container, err/tol <= 0.8; first-session gate: the full pipeline within 1.4x of its own step-0 skeleton time at 64,56,56 Refuted if: kill line (hardware premise): the step-0 memory-only skeleton at 64,56,56 takes > 200 us rented, i.e. the stored-h stream cannot beat e4 by 20% even with free maths; otherwise build and measure the best configuration reached This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%.
